newsitem.title: GERMANY: Former Stasi boss called as witness in Wolf trial.
newsitem.headline: Former Stasi boss called as witness in Wolf trial.

text.p: The former head of communist East Germany's secret police, Erich Mielke, has been called as a witness in the trial of legendary East German spymaster Markus Wolf, a court spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
The court itself called Mielke, whom East Germans dubbed "The Master of Fear" when he was head of the notorious Ministry for State Security (Stasi), to testify on March 19.

But the spokeswoman said it was not clear whether the 89-year-old would be deemed healthy enough to make the journey from Berlin to Duesseldorf, where the trial opened earlier this month, or whether he would be prepared to speak in court.
Mielke was released from jail in 1995 having served two thirds of a six-year sentence imposed in October 1993 for killing two policemen in 1931 while he was a communist street fighter.

He was also charged with manslaughter in connection with the killing of refugees as they tried to escape to West Germany across the heavily fortified East German border, but he was considered too old and ill to stand trial.

Wolf, 73, went on trial this month on charges of abduction, coercion and causing bodily harm in connection with kidnappings carried out by the Stasi during Wolf's more than 30 years as head of East Berlin's foreign intelligence network.

The trial is a last bid by prosecutors to bring him to book after Germany's highest court overturned a 1993 treason conviction two years ago saying Wolf could not be convicted for spying on what was then a foreign country -- West Germany.
This time prosecutors have charged Wolf with crimes which were also criminal under East German law.
